dedupe_keys.name: superwell global groundwater extraction volumes and costs six scenarios

description: This Pacific Northwest National Laboratory dataset contains Superwell simulations of groundwater extraction and associated costs across a global 0.5-degree grid. It combines two ponded-depth targets, 0.3 and 0.6 metres, with depletion limits of 5, 25 and 40 percent to produce six scenarios. Tables report pumping years, aquifer and geographic attributes, extractable volumes, drawdown, well numbers, energy demand and capital or operating costs. They can supply groundwater availability and cost assumptions for water-supply and coupled water-energy simulations. The time axis follows each grid cell’s simulated pumping lifetime, not a historical monitoring period. Zenodo provides compressed CSV outputs and smaller examples free under CC BY 4.0; its metadata explicitly cites the MSD-LIVE dataset named by the GMD paper. A limitation is that these are conditional model outputs, sensitive to aquifer properties and depletion assumptions. The output bundle is documented as several gigabytes after extraction. Superwell is a separate G5 model draft; no directly related existing catalogue record was established. No data files were downloaded.
